Availability of a Markov Chain

Source: R/04_avail.R
avail.Rd

Compute the discrete-time availability function of a system whose degradation/repair dynamics are modeled by a finite-state Markov chain. Availability at time \(t\) is defined as $$ A(t) = \Pr\{ X_t \in \mathcal{U} \} $$ where \(X_t\) is the state of the chain at time \(t\) and \(\mathcal{U}\) is the set of up (operational) states.

Usage

avail(x, time, up)

Arguments

x

An object of class MarkovChain.

time

A nonempty positive integer vector giving the discrete time points \(t\) at which availability \(A(t)\) is evaluated.

up

Integer-valued numeric vector of state positions or character vector of state names giving the operational states. Missing values are not allowed. Duplicates are ignored; empty and full state sets are valid.

Value

A numeric vector of the same length as time, where the \(j\)-th element is the probability that the system is available (in an up state) at time[j].

Details

For each time \(t\), the function computes $$ A(t) = a P^t \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{U}}, $$ where \(a\) is the initial distribution, \(P\) is the transition matrix, and \(\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{U}}\) is the indicator vector of the operational states.

Duplicate values in up are ignored. Powers are computed by repeated real matrix multiplication with Ppowers().

See also

MarkovChain(), Ppowers(), vcov_avail()

Examples

P <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
x <- MarkovChain(c(0.4, 0.6), P)
avail(x, time = 1:3, up = 1L)
#> [1] 0.500 0.550 0.575
vcov_avail(x, time = 3L, up = 1L)
#> [1] 0.5953125
